#1769. David Raya injury update as expert explains if Arsenal star can play against Man City

Arsenal hope David Raya has avoided a serious shoulder injury but their goalkeeper is still likely to be a doubt for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.

The Spain international injured his shoulder in a rather innocuous incident during last weekend’s draw with Newcastle United, making contact with William Osula while claiming a cross.

Raya was left in considerable pain with Sky Sports forced to apologise for initially playing down the incident. The former Brentford star trudged off the pitch clutching his arm to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, who started in his place in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Raya was visibly distressed on Saturday night and it prompted huge concerns over the man who has been so pivotal to Arsenal’s rise to the summit of English football. While boasting the most formidable squad in the Premier League, Raya is simply irreplaceable.

The outlook was brighter this week with Mikel Arteta revealing his goalkeeper will not require surgery.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment,’ Arteta told the media earlier this week.

‘The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.’

Arsenal have not disclosed any specific details over the injury but it seems clear at this stage Raya is not facing the sort of layoff that kept Nick Pope out for over four months after he suffered a dislocated shoulder in 2023.

They will hope any layoff is a short-term one heading into the festive period with a trip to the Etihad now looming large this weekend. Kepa was trusted with a starting role against City in the Carabao Cup final ahead of Raya back in March, having started in every previous round of the competition, but was at fault at Wembley that day as Pep Guardiola’s side claimed the first silverware of the season.

There was plenty of panic on Saturday night as Raya made his way off the pitch at St James’ Park. While Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes are pivotal figures, there is simply no replacing their no1.

Pundits lined up fearing the worst for Arsenal at the weekend with Jamie Redknapp suggesting any absence will ‘change everything for Arsenal for a while.’

Read more on what he and Arsenal legend Ian Wright said on the night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

While Arteta trusts Kepa, getting Raya back as soon as possible will be vital. Arsenal have sent reassuring messages this week but having him back in time for this weekend is likely to be a big ask.

‘It is so hard to tell how long he may be out for, we would want to know the full diagnosis,’ Stephen Smith, CEO and founder of Kitman Labs which specialises in injury welfare and performance analytics, told Metro.

‘All we have to use is the replay of the incident and how he looked coming off the pitch and he did look in incredible pain. He looked like someone who had dislocated his shoulder playing rugby. My guess is that if there was that much pain and discomfort immediately, this weekend would be too soon. That said, looking back at how innocuous it was, you would hope the length of his absence  would be the small number of weeks range.’

Arsenal have a relatively clean bill of health elsewhere in the squad with Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka their only other absences.

Saka’s latest injury is likely to keep him out until Christmas with spells on the sidelines becoming increasingly regular for the winger.

Are a growing number of knocks coupled with the years of unrelenting game time taking their toll on the England international?

Read our deep dive into Saka’s injury history as the experts tell us if Arsenal have something to really be concerned with.

Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the league and don’t play a game outside of London until mid-January. But their run of fixtures in December could provide the most thorough examination of their ability to defend their crown this season.

The month starts with a trip to Raya’s old club Brentford, followed by the north London derby against a rejuvenated Tottenham. Real Madrid then come to town in the Champions League before Arsenal host Bournemouth, who walked away with the win on their last visit to north London. They then host Manchester United in their last game before Christmas.

Arteta will be expected to shed more light on Raya’s recovery period when he speaks to the press on Friday with he and his staff now likely to have a clear picture of what the injury is after further scans this week.

Raya is perhaps the most athletic goalkeeper in the league and ensuring he is able to reach his spectacular physical levels will be key in the coming days and weeks.

Smith explained the process will involve four stages to ensure Raya is pain-free before he returns to action.

‘Finding out surgery is not needed so quickly was very encouraging. My guess is after the second scan this week they will know exactly what it is at this point,’ he said.

‘In terms of recovery time, it all depends on exactly what it is. If it was a slight subluxation then they will be looking at letting that rest, recover and become pain free, allowing it to get a range of motion back before doing a small amount of strengthening work and get him back out there.

‘If it something closer to a rotator cuff strain it may take a little longer. Typically what they are looking at in this situation comes in four stages. The first is settling the pain and protecting the joint, the second is getting full range back, the third is rebuilding strength around it and fourth, which can take a bit more time, is position-specific loading.

‘When you think about the shoulder and what a goalkeeper is required to do – all their diving and landing, catching overhead, distributing the ball – it’s pretty demanding on the shoulder. So even if it is on the lower end of the scale from a structural damage perspective, it is still likely to require time to make sure he is capable of doing all that.

‘The first 48 hours will have been the most painful. But throughout the rehab process, they won’t want him to be sore. If he’s sore, that means potentially they aren’t giving it enough time. So they will want him to feel really comfortable and really strong.’

#1765. Ian Holloway SACKED by Swindon two days after trying to confront angry fans in feisty full-time scenes at Newport - with Premier League cult hero claiming club's training ground is haunted

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW

Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger)

The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25

'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'

Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

'It's devastating,' said Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just said to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'

Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'

Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway said on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'

#1761. Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He said: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”

Tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

“It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

“So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I said, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”

Tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”

On Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always said he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”

“It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a new level of pressure.”

Tuchel has now claimed that people say the 6-4 against France is “maybe one of their best experiences (watching football) ever”.

Again, not something anyone has said to me. Where is Tuchel finding these people?!

Tuchel on Alexander-Arnold: “He comes as a right back.” Sounds like he agrees with Mourinho that the Real Madrid player is not a midfielder.

Tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

Tuchel says the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”

Tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s important to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

#1759. Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:52, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 04:58

The City Ground will be the backdrop for a clash that will impact the race for Europe and the relegation battle in the Premier League table, when Chelsea visit Nottingham Forest on Friday.

The Garibaldis are hoping to bounce back from defeat at the weekend, while the Blues are desperate to avoid a third loss in a row.

Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest have endured a dire campaign to date, and they will be fighting to stay out of the bottom three this week.

The Tricky Trees are currently 17th with nine points to their name, only above 18th-placed Sunderland on goal difference, as well as a single point ahead of 19th-placed Manchester United, and just two clear of bottom club Crystal Palace.

Glasner's side shocked the Premier League by beating Manchester City 3-1 on November 7, courtesy of a sixth-minute opener from Cunha and a brace from Liam Delap.

However, Forest failed to build on what was just their second win of the top-flight season, falling to a 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth on Saturday.

That loss marked the sixth time that the Garibaldis have blanked in 11 league matches this term, and only Sunderland have scored fewer than their tally of nine goals so far.

Meanwhile, Xabi Alonso arrived at Chelsea knowing that he had his work cut out to right the ship, but the Londoners travel to the City Ground in particularly poor form.

On Saturday, the Blues were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds United at Stamford Bridge, a stunning result in its own right made worse by the fact Emmanuel Emegha had given Chelsea the lead midway through the first half.

That defeat was a fourth in five games for Alonso's side, who were also beaten 1-0 by struggling Sunderland at the Stadium of Light prior to the international break.

Adding to the growing concern at the club is the fact that Chelsea have now conceded 20 goals in the top flight, meaning that promoted Coventry City and Ipswich Town are the only teams outside of the relegation zone to have let in more this term.

Now eighth in the Premier League table with 16 points, the Blues are five behind fourth-placed Liverpool, but still have fifth-placed Bournemouth in their sights just two points in front.

However, Alonso will also be looking over his shoulder on Friday, given that his side are within reach of every club down to 13th-placed Newcastle United, and another defeat could see them drop into the bottom half.

Forest are without Nicolo Savona once again as he recovers from a knee injury, though Daniel Munoz should be on hand to start at right wing-back, flanking Glasner's three-man defence.

The Tricky Trees are also missing midfielder Nicolas Dominguez, who has been dealing with a muscle injury, so Xaver Schlager and James McAtee could operate in the centre of the park on Friday.

On a more positive note, the hosts are set to welcome former Chelsea star Callum Hudson-Odoi back after he returned to training this week, and he is likely to offer additional firepower from the bench while Morgan Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye line up behind striker Liam Delap.

As for Chelsea, they have doubts about midfielder Moises Caicedo, who was forced off with a back issue against Leeds, and winger Jamie Gittens, who has returned to training but is still building fitness after his layoff.

With that in mind, Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers should start behind Emmanuel Emegha, given that talismanic centre-forward Joao Pedro is sidelined due to a thigh injury.

At the opposite end of the pitch, versatile right-back Reece James has a knee injury, left-sided defender Jorrel Hato is out with a back issue, and centre-half Maxence Lacroix is recovering from a hamstring injury.

In their absence, Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill will operate at the heart of Alonso's defence, while Josh Acheampong and Pep Chavarria start at full-back.

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Gibbs-White, Ndoye; Delap

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Henderson, Lavia; Neto, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha

Forest have struggled for goals this season, but they will be motivated by the threat of slipping into the relegation zone, and given optimism by the visitors' poor form.

Chelsea arrive on the back of four defeats in five games, desperate to find their feet amidst a spate of injuries, though it would come as no surprise to see the Blues drop points once again.

#1757. Frosinone boss Alvini content with aggressive approach vs. Milan despite ‘naive’ mistakes

Frosinone head coach Massimiliano Alvini has admitted that his side simply gave AC Milan too many opportunities.

It has been a very positive return to the top flight for Frosinone so far, given that a point last night at San Siro would have seen them move back into the European places. However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

“Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”

“We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

“There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I said before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

“He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are important players on the other side who can cause problems.”

“It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

“Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”

#1756. Bayern Munich slammed as 'despicable' and accused of 'co-ordinated' plot to undermine Jamal Musiala after club chief questioned star's contract due to his health issues - with Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand backing the youngster

Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026

Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level

Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen said in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'

'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'

The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he said. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'

'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'

Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig)

The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication

Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend

Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health issues Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'

'Money has become more important than the person, and that is unacceptable.'

Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how important 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg said, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical issues.

'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'

By Lewis Nolan | 25 Nov 2026 23:55

Liverpool are seriously considering re-signing Jarell Quansah from Bayer Leverkusen in 2027, the latest report has claimed.

Andoni Iraola's side emerged as 3-0 winners against Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, with the Merseysiders keeping a second consecutive clean sheet.

Quansah is a strong passer of the ball ane has demonstrated in the past that he is capable of coming out on top in battles in the air, though he has struggled to settle this season.

In the 2026-27 Bundesliga, the centre-back has only completed 42.3 passes per match and has won just 32% of his aerial duels, something that may be a major concern to Liverpool given he is 6ft 3in.

The 23-year-old completed 52.8 passes per game last season in the league, while he also won 60% of his aerial duels.

There are concerns about Quansah's recovery defending and temperament inside the box, so perhaps Liverpool should look elsewhere in the summer for the heir to Van Dijk.

The unfortunate reality for Liverpool is that they will have to become accustomed to life without Van Dijk sooner rather than later.

However, there is nothing to suggest based on his current form that the 35-year-old cannot continue to play at the highest level for at least another season.

As long as Van Dijk can continue to dominate attackers and use his immense recovery pace, then Liverpool should look to extend their captain's contract.

#1753. Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as new signing confirmed

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Teenage defender Isaac Allen has confirmed that he has joined Tottenham after leaving rivals West Ham in the summer.

In August, reports claimed that Spurs had beaten Arsenal to Allen’s signature, and the 15-year-old has now announced the move on social media.

The England U15s captain wrote in a post on Instagram: “Happy to be signed with Tottenham.”

Allen, who can operate either at centre-back or in defensive midfield, is regarded as one of the most promising young talents in England and his arrival continues Spurs’ busy youth recruitment strategy.

During last month’s Fan Advisory Board (FAB) meeting, the club confirmed that as part of their commitment to the academy, they had actively recruited players aged 16 and under and invested in the U10 to U17 age groups.

Allen is the latest highly-rated teenage talent to arrive at Hotspur Way, with Cole Ramsey (19), Kwasi Senyah (16), Gabriel Rigg (15) and Jake Maloney (14) all signing in recent months.

Tottenham are understood to be pairing football development with private schooling and strong professional terms once players turn 17, to beat competition from rival clubs.

The change in approach has been brought on by an acknowledgement internally that Spurs have struggled not only to offer academy players a pathway into the first team, but also to maximise their value by selling them on if they don’t believe they have a future at the club.

Tottenham hope to highlight the progression of 18-year-old winger Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut in the Premier League against Ipswich last weekend before being handed a new long-term contract, as an example of the pathway into the first team.

Meanwhile, the success of the current Championship leading goalscorer Will Lankshear, who joined Middlesbrough in a deal worth up to £20million in the summer, showcases Spurs’ willingness to find productive permanent solutions for players who can’t be guaranteed regular first-team minutes after coming through the academy.

#1752. Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

It was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it quickly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

Both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”

It was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another new signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”

Gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “big lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta said. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

“It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

“It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta said. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always important to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”

Two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a big lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge."

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

We won the ball high up and attacked really fast. After the last two wins we are full of confidence and wanted to finish really strong before the international break.

I feel really good. I can’t complain. I just try to help the team when I can. I really enjoy life in Brighton, I’m loving it.

Everton up to fifth but they made hard work of that against Ipswich’s 10 men, but Thierno Barry’s goal proves the difference. Barry unfortunate that his second did not stand because of a contentious offside check.

Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Hull are knocking on the door at St James’ Park, and Newcastle are hanging on to their lead rather than pressing for a third goal.

The forward is shown a second yellow card for diving, and Ipswich’s hopes appear to be dwindling at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

The home team are pressing high and all over Arsenal in the early stages. Raya has just made a save to deny Kostoulas.

Brighton have started brilliantly against the champions. They are hunting like wolves, pressing Arsenal with remarkable intensity. We have played seven minutes and I don’t think the ball has left Arsenal’s half.

Big chance for Everton to take the lead, but after great skill to turn his man at the edge of the box Brennan Johnson shoots wide with only the goalkeeper to beat.

The perfect start for Newcastle with all their injuries: Joe Willock has put the home side in a strong position against Hull with a clean strike inside three minutes.

We are under way at the Amex, St James’ Park and the Hill Dickinson.

Another famous face in the stands at Hill Dickinson Stadium today but this time it’s not about politicians. #1749. ‘Apology FC’: Manchester United fans make clear demand after Sporting referee ‘robbery’

Manchester United fans have it out at referee Szymon Marciniak and UEFA over a host of controversial decisions during their 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League.

The 2022 World Cup final ref pointed to the spot for a soft Sporting penalty in the first half, though Luis Suarez’s spot kick was saved by Senne Lammens. Minutes later Lammens went from hero to zero when rushing out of his goal and taking out Maximiliano Araujo for another penalty. Suarez made amends from 12 yards.

Amad Diallo thought he had equalised, only for his goal to be ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up, which earned the midfielder a yellow card after some vigorous protests.

Man Utd received a penalty of their own early in the second half also bordered on soft; Lisandro Martinez going down very easily after Eduardo Quaresma’s clumsy challenge.

Bruno Fernandes converted and then two minutes later benefitted from a divot of his own creation, albeit inadvertently, to hand Man Utd the lead, when he low, driven shot flicked up off the pitch to beat keeper Kaique Pereira.

A chaos continued when a Lammens howler saw Sporting equaliser, the keeper failing to deal with a cross to allow Suarez to instinctively, and acrobatically, finish from close range.

And then, at the other end of the pitch, an extremely similar scenario occurred as Pereira palmed the ball into his own net at a Man Utd corner for what appeared to be the winner.

Referee Marciniak initially awarded the goal, but VAR ordered a pitchside review which saw Martinez and Patrick Dorgu penalised for a foul on the keeper. There was still time for a red card as Tielemans was shown a second yellow for a late, studs up challenge.

The performance stirred up plenty of frustrations among the fanbase, especially in light of Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool which was later overturned by the Premier League.

There were plenty of fans, both with an affiliation to Man utd and not, claiming a “robbery”.

A Man Utd fan said one of the decisions “boiled his blood”, while others were left waiting for another apology after the Yoro debacle.

#1747. ‘Disgrace’: Manchester United legend lets rip after Champions League controversy

Ex-Manchester United star Ashley Young labelled the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak during Wednesday’s chaotic Champions League draw with Sporting as a “disgrace”.

Marciniak was at the centre of multiple controversial decisions in a dramatic 2-2 league phase tie in Lisbon, awarding three penalties, ruling out two Man Utd goals and sending off midfielder Youri Tielemans in stoppage time.

New Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino claimed that his side had been “punished” by the officials, going on to say that it was “impossible” to understand how the decisions were reached.

‘Apology FC’: Man Utd fans make clear demand after referee ‘robbery’

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Young held a similar position, with the former winger left searching for words when speaking about Marciniak’s display.

The ex-United captain said on BBC Radio 5 Live: “The referee’s performance was just simply… wow.

“The decisions that he gave… Youri Tielemans getting booked, to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

“The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the ‘keeper.

“The ‘keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace.”

United fans would have been further irked by the decision to rule out their potential late winner, as Sporting’s equaliser came in a similar fashion. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens dropped a high ball under light pressure, allowing Luis Suarez to convert with an improvised bicycle kick.

However, talkSPORT pundit Gabby Agbonlahor believes the reaction to the refereeing controversies has been overblown.

He said on Thursday morning: “Manchester United fans, just get on with it. You didn’t deserve to win the game.

“Did the referee make a couple of mistakes? Yes, he did. But come on. Manchester United fans - first they’re moaning about the owners, next they’re moaning about chief executives, [Omar] Berrada, [Jason] Wilcox. Now it’s referees every game, it’s VAR every game.

“How about - you didn’t deserve to win the game? The referee didn’t make Lisandro Martinez make a stupid challenge to give away the first penalty that gets saved.

“The referee didn’t make [Noussair] Mazraoui come in so tight to the centre-half and allow the [Sporting] left-back flying forward.

“The referee didn’t make Lammens come out to no man’s land. I don’t know what he’s doing. I don’t know what he’s going to achieve running out there.

“The referee didn’t make Lammens have chocolate wrists and drop the ball when no one is on him.”

The draw with Sporting leaves United 19th in the Champions League table, with three games remaining in this season’s league phase.

Tielemans’ red card means the Belgian will miss their next European fixture - a home tie with Bundesliga outfit RB Leipzig on December 8.

Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form

Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games

This morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

Like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

Every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

Let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

Anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

Believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge

We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

He’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

Which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

Palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

For me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck

WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

Striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

We have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

Emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

Not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

Alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities

I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

As for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali has returned to training ahead of Tottenham’s visit to Sunderland this weekend, but Savio is expected to miss out.

Tonali missed Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last Saturday due to illness, as Roberto De Zerbi’s side earned three points on their return from the international break, but is set to be available for selection when Spurs travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

Savio, meanwhile, was named on the bench against Ipswich, having missed the last four games with a muscular injury. The 22-year-old was introduced in the second half, but lasted just 26 minutes before he had to come off injured.

Savio was visibly upset as he headed down the tunnel, and De Zerbi confirmed he had suffered a recurrence of the same injury that had kept him out for the last six weeks.

"I'm sorry for Savio's injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him. He's a crucial player for us,” De Zerbi said in his post-match press conference.

“He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season."

Savio is expected to join fellow wingers Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk on the sidelines, meaning teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut against Ipswich, could be in line for more minutes.

Fears over an injury to Omar Marmoush have been allayed after the forward was spotted in training footage.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo is expected to be available for selection again after returning from a calf injury. Tosin was fit to play against Ipswich, but De Zerbi chose not to take any unnecessary risks.

Rodrigo Bentancur could also return to the starting lineup, having been named on the bench against Ipswich after returning late from international duty.

#1743. Man City get appeal verdict update ahead of Arsenal clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Manchester City have been given an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges ahead of this weekend’s huge title clash with Arsenal.

City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018. The commission also found the Man City had made "concerted efforts to stop and frustrate" the investigation.

The club have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should the appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League, all the while Man City‘s form on the pitch has suffered a dip.

City have won just one of their last five games across all competitions, and have lost three of their last four in the Premier League to see their title hopes handed a huge blow. Arsenal is up next on Sunday in a game Erling Haaland has already described as their “toughest of the season”.

Amid the on-pitch struggles, financial expert Stefan Borson, who previously worked as a financial advisor to City, expects there to be clarity sooner rather than later over the club’s off-pitch concerns.

"We're told that it will be mid-December,” Borson said, regarding the appeal hearing, on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan and Simon Jordan.

“Because of the way the days fall, that's likely to start on the 12th.

"It's likely to go for between five and 10 days, it seems, and therefore finish before Christmas. And then we wait for a decision. Ordinarily, that decision would take quite some time.

"I suspect that certainly the Premier League want to get it expedited so they get a decision and can then have the sanction hearing and the sanction appeal, which is inevitable either way, in before the end of the season so they can effectively sanction City and punish them this season."

Borson suggested a timetable may already have been agreed, with the Premier League keen to avoid further legal complications.

"In the rulebook that came out at the start of the season, the rules changed and you had an expedited timetable. In any event, a case like City's and an appeal like City's would never fall within the standardised timetable.

"I think most likely the parties have ultimately agreed some form of timetable which means that any argument from City in the future about the process goes away.

"The last thing the Premier League will want is to give City another reason to take legal action under Rule X or otherwise and to say, actually the whole appeal process, not only was the old process flawed but we didn't even have a fair appeal. Because if they do that, we're back to square one."

#1742. Portland Timbers vs Dallas - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 26 Nov 2026 01:21, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 01:22

Needing a victory to keep their MLS season alive, the Portland Timbers will host Dallas in game two of that best-of-three series on Saturday at Providence Park.

The opener went to Los Toros in Frisco, 3-0, putting them one win away from the Western Conference semi-finals for the first time since 2022.

For the second successive campaign, the Timbers face a must-win situation heading into game two of the playoffs after lacking decisiveness in the attacking third last Saturday.

Portland have not made it beyond the opening round of the playoffs since their run to the MLS Cup final in 2021, losing to New York City FC on penalties that year.

They are now 12-10-8 all-time in post-season outings, while winning just one of their last seven playoff games in normal time.

That said, Marti Cifuentes has seen his side lose just one of their last six league fixtures at Providence Park, winning those last two matches and scoring three goals both times.

In addition to that, this club have gone on to win their last two post-season matches at home, while suffering just one playoff defeat this decade at Providence Park in 90 minutes.

The Timbers have never lost a playoff home game versus Dallas in normal time, though their last post-season win against them at Providence Park occurred in 2015 (3-1).

After a cagey opening 45 minutes in game one, Dallas took command in the second half last week, putting themselves in the driver’s seat to advance.

Whatever Eric Quill is saying to this group at half-time, the message has been well received, with his team outscoring opponents by a combined 6-1 margin in the second half of their last two games.

A triumph on Saturday would snap a three-match MLS winless run for the Texas club away from home and mark their first playoff victory as the visitors since beating the Timbers on penalties in Portland in 2020.

Since that triumph, Dallas have failed to score in four of their last five post-season affairs which took place outside of Frisco.

In 2026, they have conceded in all but three MLS road outings, while allowing three or more goals on four separate occasions.

Los Toros can extend their winning run versus Portland to three matches on Saturday, while they are unbeaten in eight successive meetings against them.

Portland Timbers Major League Soccer form:

Do not expect to see Juan David Mosquera on the field for the Timbers Saturday as he recovers from a foot and ankle issue, while Zac McGraw has a sore back, Brandon Bye is dealing with a knee injury and Alex Bonetig is doubtful due to a shoulder strain.

Cole Bassett and Kristoffer Velde were the most dangerous Portland players in game one, each with three shots, while James Pantemis made five stops in a losing effort.

At Dallas, Anderson Julio is questionable for this match because of a lower-body injury after sitting out in the opening game of this series.

Joaquin Valiente registered his first career playoff brace in game one, with Sam Sarver scoring his first MLS post-season goal in that victory.

Portland Timbers possible starting lineup:

Pantemis; Hernandez, K. Miller, Waterman, Fory; Bassett, Chara, Da Costa; Velde, Janssen, Lassiter

Daniel; Johansson, Urhoghide, Moore, Norris; Valiente, Kaick, Ramiro, Binyamin; Musa, Sarver

Dallas tend to sit back away from home, and while their defensive shape will be tough to break down, we believe the Timbers' attacking depth and desperation will keep them alive.

#1740. Martin Odegaard critics are wrong - Arsenal must give him what he deserves

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

A quick glance at two contrasting stats sums up exactly where Arsenal’s shortcomings lie at the moment.

Mikel Arteta’s side are still in fine shape to progress straight through to the last 16 as one of the top-eight sides in the Champions League. Only the Gunners, holders Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid remain unbeaten in this season’s competition.

However, it could have been so much better, after an extraordinarily wasteful display in the draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night. Arsenal registered 30 shots, but only four on target and they scored just once.

It should have been so much more for Martin Odegaard, too. He has registered only one assist in Europe this season, ranking him 45th in the competition for that metric.

And yet for expected assists, per FotMob, Odegaard ranks top across the entire Champions League. Above Nico Paz, who has five assists to his name, and Lamine Yamal, who has three.

Arsenal have had no issue creating chances. Against Dortmund, Odegaard laid on nine of them, the most by any player in a Champions League match this season.

That was just the second time this decade that an Arsenal player has created more than five chances in a Champions League match. The other example? Odegaard against Napoli in September.

The discourse around Odegaard is often hypercritical. That, to an extent, is understandable. He has been the captain and creative heartbeat of the team in a period in which, for all it has been successful, there have been ongoing questions surrounding the attack.

It is perhaps also a hangover from the last two seasons, when injuries hampered Odegaard and he was well off his best. Frustration towards him built and some minds appear to have been made up.

However, the criticism that he does not deliver consistently enough just does not hold up to scrutiny this season.

Man City get appeal verdict update ahead of Arsenal clash

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal

Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as signing confirmed

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

From the moment Odegaard returned to the club in the summer after a strong World Cup with Norway, he has looked back to his best. That started with his sublime goal against Manchester City in the Community Shield and has continued since.

For all there have been some notable exceptions, Arsenal have on the whole played much better football this season. They have been far more free-flowing and fluid in attack.

Odegaard has been central to that. Along with his chance creation stats in Europe, Odegaard is also second for expected assists in the Premier League.

He is taking more responsibility in front of goal, too. Odegaard is Arsenal’s top scorer this season and is only one league goal shy of his combined tally from the last two seasons.

If there has been a dip in Arsenal’s attack from the start of this season, that is not down to Odegaard. Bukayo Saka, who was displaying far better goalscoring instincts, suffering a quad injury, and Kai Havertz’s performance levels dropping significantly are far more relevant explanations.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard

Odegaard has been the most consistent forward player. It is not just the chances created or even the goals, but his influence in all facets of Arsenal’s game as almost an extension of Arteta on the pitch. He is the leader of the press, and that led to the winning goal against Liverpool at Anfield earlier this month.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard. It is not an exaggeration to say that Viktor Gyokeres should have scored another three goals against Dortmund from chances created by Odegaard alone.

The Gunners are not clinical enough but that is not the fault of the player creating the chances. Nor is it a coaching issue. Arteta could not have done more to deliver a win against Dortmund.

The problem is a personnel one. The quality of Arsenal’s attackers does not come close to matching the level in every other position in the squad. At least one top-class winger signing is required, along with a new striker.

It was clear at the end of last season that significant upgrades were needed. Instead, Arsenal sold three forwards and signed only Christos Tzolis.

That is the big failure and where the fingers should be pointing. Not at Odegaard for occasionally taking too many touches or making a wrong decision on the counter.

Odegaard’s contract situation adds another factor to the debate over his role in the team. He is nearing the final 18 months of his current deal.

Talks have not yet begun over an extension, Odegaard revealed during the international break, but that should be a no-brainer for Arsenal.

That will require the club to make another significant financial commitment, following on from several other new contracts for key players, but it is still a far cheaper alternative to trying to sign a replacement of Odegaard’s quality.

Securing Odegaard’s future should be the club’s next top priority, swiftly followed by then delivering him the forwards he deserves.
